summary: This document reclassifies several TCP extensions that never saw widespread use to Historic status. The affected RFCs are RFC 1072, RFC 1106, RFC 1110, RFC 1145, RFC 1146, RFC 1379, RFC 1644, and RFC 1693. The document itself is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo changes the official status of several TCP extension documents that had not seen widespread use. It also asks IANA to mark their associated TCP option numbers obsolete.

subtitle: Moves several TCP extensions that lacked widespread use to Historic status.

tldr.problem: Several TCP extension RFCs had not seen widespread use, and their Historic status was not reflected in the RFC database and relevant IANA registries.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC directs the RFC Editor to mark eight extension RFCs Historic and directs IANA to mark listed TCP option numbers obsolete.
tldr.outcome: It records the status changes and notes reported security issues for T/TCP. It also updates RFC 4614, according to the unit metadata.

today: RFC 6247 is listed as Informational and updates RFC 4614, according to the unit metadata. It obsoletes eight TCP extension RFCs.

sections.title: Why These Extensions Changed Status
sections.content:
TCP has accumulated proposed extensions, and several had never seen widespread deployment. An earlier TCP roadmap already described some of them as Historic, but did not direct the RFC Editor and IANA to update their official records.

This memo's purpose is to make those status and registry changes. It points readers to the roadmap for the reasons behind the original assessments.
sections.plainLanguage: Some TCP extension ideas were not widely used, but their official records still needed updating. This memo directs the organizations maintaining those records to make the changes.

sections.title: RFCs Marked Historic
sections.content:
The RFC Editor marked RFCs 1072, 1106, 1110, 1145, 1146, 1379, 1644, and 1693 as Historic. They concern long-delay paths, big windows and NAKs, alternate checksums, TCP transactions, and partial-order service.

The unit metadata for this RFC also lists those eight documents as obsoleted by RFC 6247.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo moves eight TCP extension RFCs to Historic status. They cover several different proposed additions to TCP.

sections.title: TCP Option Registry Changes
sections.content:
IANA marked TCP option numbers 6, 7, and 9 through 15 as obsolete in the TCP Option Kind Numbers registry, with a reference to this memo.

The RFC also notes that T/TCP, described by RFCs 1379 and 1644, had reported security issues.
sections.plainLanguage: IANA records the associated TCP option numbers as obsolete. The memo also points out reported security issues in the TCP transaction extensions.

references.text: Duke, M., Braden, R., Eddy, W., and E. Blanton, "A Roadmap for Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) Specification Documents", RFC 4614, September 2006.
